cases.name: an-assertion-that-holds-changes-nothing
cases.description: The first thing an assertion must do is not exist as far as the data is concerned. These two configs are the same run — one carries <assert>, one does not — and the lines below are what BOTH produce, so an implementation that drew a value while evaluating the condition, or that let an extra <env> child shift the keys its columns derive from, is caught by a diff rather than by a passing check. The condition itself is true: seventy percent of ten rows is seven, and the parent filter is the only thing standing between the percentage and the column.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="10" seed="s" local="en"><sequence name="Kind"><gen type="text" value="a,b" percent="70,30"/></sequence><sequence name="Amount" parent="Kind.a"><gen type="number" value="1..100"/></sequence><sequence name="Rows"><gen type="stat" of="Amount" op="count"/></sequence><assert that="Rows == 7" says="every a-row carries an amount"/></env><block><line><data>${{Kind}},${{Amount}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: the-same-run-without-the-assertion
cases.description: The twin of the case above, written out rather than described, because a claim about two configs is only checked when both are run. Every line here must match its neighbour's exactly.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="10" seed="s" local="en"><sequence name="Kind"><gen type="text" value="a,b" percent="70,30"/></sequence><sequence name="Amount" parent="Kind.a"><gen type="number" value="1..100"/></sequence><sequence name="Rows"><gen type="stat" of="Amount" op="count"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{Kind}},${{Amount}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: _total-is-whole-run-constant
cases.description: The one built-in an assertion may read. _count is deliberately not: it says which row you are on, which is exactly what an assertion must not depend on — a condition that reads it would report on row 0 and call the run verified.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="4" seed="s" local="en"><sequence name="N"><gen type="number" value="1..9"/></sequence><assert that="_total == 4" says="the run is four rows"/></env><block><line><data>${{N}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: a-one-value-column-counts-as-whole-run-constant
cases.description: The rule is about the DATA, not about the spelling. A stat column is constant by construction, but so is a text column with one value in it, and refusing that would make the rule a list of approved generator types rather than a statement about the run. Every implementation therefore has to READ the column rather than look at how it was written.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="3" seed="s" local="en"><sequence name="Env"><gen type="text" value="prod"/></sequence><sequence name="N"><gen type="number" value="1..9"/></sequence><assert that="Env == 'prod'" says="the fixture is built for production"/></env><block><line><data>${{Env}}-${{N}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: several-assertions-all-hold
cases.description: Two conditions over two stat columns, plus arithmetic between them. Nothing here fails, so what is pinned is that a run carrying several assertions still produces exactly its data — and that reading a name twice, across two assertions, does not consume anything the second reader then misses.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="10" seed="s" local="en"><sequence name="Plan"><gen type="text" value="free,paid" percent="80,20"/></sequence><sequence name="Paid" parent="Plan.paid"><gen type="number" value="1..9"/></sequence><sequence name="Free" parent="Plan.free"><gen type="number" value="1..9"/></sequence><sequence name="P"><gen type="stat" of="Paid" op="count"/></sequence><sequence name="F"><gen type="stat" of="Free" op="count"/></sequence><assert that="P + F == _total" says="every row belongs to exactly one plan"/><assert that="P == 2" says="a fifth of ten rows is two"/></env><block><line><data>${{Plan}}:${{Paid}}${{Free}}</data></line></block></tdc>
